about_page_description: 22-year-old game audio student at DAE Belgium. Piano background, built audio for 4 games, now building tools and experimenting with procedural audio generation.
intro: 22. Third-year audio student at DAE in Belgium. Did audio for 4 games so far.
story_1: Started piano when I was six. Twelve years of lessons. Around high school I got curious about why sound works, not just how to play it. That's when I switched to math and physics and started writing Python scripts to fix broken audio files.
story_2: At DAE I built a beatbox classifier when the off-the-shelf ML models were too slow. Wrote Wwise repair scripts because fixing references by hand after every Perforce merge got old fast. Did audio for 4 student games using Wwise, MetaSounds, and FMOD.
story_3: For my thesis I'm building a Unity thing that generates game audio in real-time with the ElevenLabs API. Tried caching to speed it up. Still figuring out how to make it not break when the network lags.
pull_quote: If the player can't hear the enemy because the ambient is too loud, that's not a design choice. It's a bug.
approach_1: Most of my work starts with something breaking. Footsteps playing on the wrong surface. A SoundBank eating twice the memory budget. That's when you learn what actually matters — when four players share one screen and one audio budget, you cut what doesn't need to be there.
approach_2: I build tools when I have to do the same annoying task twice. Wwise kept breaking after pulls, so I wrote a script to fix it. Now the team uses it. Same with the Unreal Engine Rebuilder. If it wastes time, automate it.
cta_text: Looking for a game audio internship in 2026. 3-6 months, EU passport, can relocate.
